access: Humanitarian vehicle access was possible on both observed routes. One route was paved and in good condition and the other dirt but passable; no road obstacles were observed and both light vehicles and trucks could access Ntamba.
completeness: Indicative - 4 KIIs, 13 purposive HESPER interviews (10 complete, 3 incomplete) and 2 structured observations. Findings are not statistically representative; final verified alert-linked caseload is 93 people.
rationale: The RNA identifies several important household-level food, shelter/NFI, WASH and protection concerns, but the final verified alert-linked caseload was only 93 people and the purposive household findings cannot be interpreted as prevalence across the full caseload. Operational access remained feasible, services were present, observations described a generally calm environment, and no immediate life-threatening condition was established. Moderate is therefore retained at RNA stage.

arrival_locations: Ntamba IDP site and Muadi host community
origin_locations: Mitope and Chinda, and Mocimboa da Praia sede (Maputo, Quelimane, Diaca, Chinda, Mitope, Pangele). In Nangade, from the villages of Ngalonga, Nambedo, Samora Machel, Namuavica, Namuembe, Lijungo, and Litingina.
movement: Mixed reactive + fear-driven; displacement remained current and most interviewed households intended to stay
relationship: September shock and wider crises affecting the district of Mocimboa da Praia and Nangade
vulnerable_groups: elders, women, and children were reported as vulnerables with urgent need of lifesaving humaniatrian assistance
needs_evidence: 21 of 22 interviewed households reported food as serious problem, 21 of 22 households reported water as serious problems and 13 of 22 households ranked among the top three, 18 of 22 households reporting shelter as a serious, 21 of 22 households reporting clothing, bedding or related household-item needs as serious, Family separation/care concerns were reported by 18 of 22 households, while 15 of 22 reported distress and 13 of 22 reported movement-related problems, Health concerns were reported by 10 of 22 households
hosting: yes - in Ntamba some of displaced people were hosted by the old IDPs in the site whilst for Muadi the hosy community were hosting the newly arrivd families
protection_evidence: Eleven of 22 households reported safety/protection as a serious problem, 13 of 22 reported movement as a serious problem, 18 of 22 reported family care/separation concerns, and 15 of 22 reported distress, worry or fear.
access: No major road-access constraint was specifically reported by the assessed households; however, the recent displacement context and security concerns may affect safe and sustained access to affected communities.
completeness: Good for main receiving area; caseload verification still needed and the movement was still ongoing
rationale: The RNA findg indicate needs on food, water and shelter as top three priority. The caseload in also above 900 HH classifying the situation as critical
